question: A 52-year-old man presents with progressive right-sided sensorineural hearing loss and right-sided tinnitus over 18 months. Pure tone audiometry confirms unilateral SNHL. Otoscopy is normal. Which imaging modality is most appropriate?

answers.text: HRCT temporal bone — it provides the best detail of the cochlea and osseous labyrinth

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: HRCT is the first choice for conductive hearing loss and bony abnormalities. For asymmetric SNHL, MRI is preferred because the primary concern is a retrocochlear lesion (especially vestibular schwannoma) which requires soft-tissue imaging.

answers.text: MRI of the internal auditory meati (IAM) with gadolinium — to exclude a retrocochlear lesion such as vestibular schwannoma

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Unilateral/asymmetric SNHL is an indication for MRI IAM with gadolinium. Vestibular schwannoma (acoustic neuroma) enhances on post-contrast T1 and is characteristically seen as an intracanalicular mass expanding the IAM. HRCT alone cannot reliably detect this lesion.

answers.text: Plain X-ray skull — it gives an overview of the petrous bone anatomy

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Plain skull X-rays are obsolete for temporal bone and hearing loss evaluation. They have been entirely replaced by CT and MRI in modern practice.

answers.text: No imaging — unilateral SNHL in a 52-year-old is most likely presbyacusis and does not require imaging

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Presbyacusis is bilateral by definition. Unilateral or asymmetric SNHL — especially progressive and associated with unilateral tinnitus — requires MRI to exclude a retrocochlear lesion. This asymmetric pattern should never be attributed to presbyacusis without imaging.

overallFeedback.feedback: The key rule: unilateral or asymmetric SNHL requires MRI IAM. HRCT is for bony/conductive pathology. Presbyacusis is always bilateral — never label asymmetric SNHL as presbyacusis without imaging.
Correct. Asymmetric SNHL = scan the nerve. MRI IAM with gadolinium is the investigation of choice to exclude vestibular schwannoma and other retrocochlear lesions.
